channel.title: Acme: Daily Reading List
channel.description: Noteworthy articles from across the web.

item.title: GAO finds barriers to a fuller National Register of Historic Places
item.description: The National Register lists more than 100,000 historically significant places, but GAO found outdated guidance and criteria that can complicate nominations, especially for tribal sites. Its recommendations call for clearer public guidance, better outreach and more explanation of how sensitive locations can remain undisclosed.

item.title: Students build 108 WordPress sites in two weeks
item.description: Free WordPress workshops in Bangladesh helped students build 108 sites across two campuses. The broader report also visits a Ugandan workshop that continued without electricity and a Costa Rican program where university students taught high schoolers, then published a guide others can reuse.

item.title: Copyright Office marks 50 years of the 1976 Copyright Act
item.description: A September 23 online event will revisit how the Copyright Act of 1976 was drafted, administered and amended, with participants who worked at the Copyright Office or on Capitol Hill. The 90-minute program offers an insider's view of the statute that reshaped U.S. copyright for modern media.

item.title: Emily St. John Mandel expands her connected universe in Exit Party
item.description: Emily St. John Mandel's new novel Exit Party blends crime and science fiction in a fractured 2031 United States while bringing back characters from earlier books. The AP profile explores how her loosely linked 'Mandelverse' lets her revisit themes of identity, impermanence and finding beauty amid disorder.

item.title: Why some 1930 works had a complicated route to the public domain
item.description: Aaron Moss surveys the major 1930 books, films, cartoons and songs that became free to use in 2026, then digs into the copyright math. Especially useful is his account of foreign films such as The Blue Angel, whose lapsed U.S. protection was restored by the URAA before expiring again at the end of 2025.

item.title: St. Augustine dig uncovers first physical evidence of a British redoubt
item.description: Archaeologists in Lincolnville found a 15-foot-wide dry moat from a British military redoubt built in 1781. It is the first of St. Augustine's seven mapped British outposts to be confirmed archaeologically, illuminating the city's often-overlooked 1763-1783 period under British rule.

item.title: Internet Archive launches project to preserve state and local government records
item.description: The Internet Archive's two-year ATLAS project will help 100 state and local government institutions preserve public records with Archive-It and Archive Vault. Built with the Council of State Archivists, it will also produce a shared portal, training materials and a summit devoted to keeping born-digital civic history accessible.

item.title: The 2026 Hugo Awards honor Harrow, El-Mohtar and Scalzi
item.description: Andrew Liptak's complete Hugo Awards rundown spotlights Alix E. Harrow's The Everlasting for Best Novel, Amal El-Mohtar's The River Has Roots for Best Novella and John Scalzi's Old Man's War for Best Series, with winners across comics, fanzines, dramatic presentations and other categories.

item.title: ServiceNow's September Creator release sharpens Studio and testing
item.description: ServiceNow's September Creator update folds the newer IDE into Studio, adds more ways to open application files there and expands automated testing with parameterized tests and test suites. It also adds domain-separation support and Build Agent improvements for developers working on Zurich and Australia releases.

item.title: Blue Beetle will return in Superman: Man of Tomorrow
item.description: Xolo Maridueña says James Gunn personally called to bring his Jaime Reyes incarnation of Blue Beetle into the new DC film universe. He will return in Superman: Man of Tomorrow, due July 9, 2027, alongside Superman, Lex Luthor, Supergirl, John Stewart and Maxima.

item.title: Hachette launches a new paperback novella line
item.description: Hachette's Union Square & Co. has launched Singularity, a paperback novella line planning 10 to 12 short books a year. Its first slate includes a new edition of Harlan Ellison's I Have No Mouth, and I Must Scream, alongside cult favorites and new work across genres.

item.title: Automattic contests WP Engine's request for sanctions
item.description: WP Engine is asking a federal court to sanction Automattic and Matt Mullenweg over allegedly unpreserved Signal, Telegram and WhatsApp messages. Automattic says extensive device collection and more than 225,000 produced documents show no relevant messages are missing. A hearing is set for Sept. 30.
